items.prompt: Which object will a magnet attract?

options.why: Plastic is not magnetic.
Wood is not magnetic.
Rubber is not magnetic.

hints: Magnets attract some metals.
Steel contains iron.
Which object is made of metal?
items.explanation: A magnet attracts things made of iron or steel. The paperclip is steel, so the magnet pulls it.

items.prompt: Sort the objects. Will a magnet attract them?
hints: Only a few metals are magnetic.
Iron and steel are magnetic.
Be careful: not every metal is magnetic.
items.explanation: Iron and steel are magnetic. Aluminium, copper and gold are metals too, but they are not magnetic, and neither are glass and plastic.

items.prompt: The north pole of one magnet is held near the north pole of another. What happens?

options.why: Different poles attract. Two north poles are the same, so they repel.
Magnets always push or pull each other when their poles are close.
Magnets keep their poles. They push apart.

hints: Both poles are the same: north.
Remember the rule for same poles and different poles.
Do same poles attract or repel?
items.explanation: Like poles repel, so two north poles push each other away. A north pole and a south pole would pull together.

items.prompt: Two south poles will ___ each other.
hints: The two poles are the same.
Same poles do not pull together.
The science word starts with r.
items.explanation: Like poles repel, which means they push each other away.

items.prompt: Three ring magnets sit on a pencil. The top magnet floats above the others. Why?

options.why: Wood is not magnetic.

options.text: The facing poles are the same, so they repel.
The top magnet is lighter than air.
options.why: Magnets are heavy. A push between the magnets holds it up.
Magnets do not attract air.

hints: Something is pushing the top magnet up.
Think about which poles push and which pull.
Are the facing poles the same or different?
items.explanation: The poles facing each other are the same, so they repel. The push holds the top magnet up in the air.

items.prompt: Rina holds a magnet under a sheet of paper. A paperclip on top moves with the magnet. What does this show?

options.why: Paper is not magnetic. The force passes through it.

options.text: A breeze is moving the paperclip.
options.why: The paperclip follows the magnet, not the air.

options.text: Magnetic force can act through paper.

options.why: The magnet did not touch the paperclip, but it still moved it.

hints: The magnet is not touching the paperclip.
Something passes through the paper.
Can a magnet pull without touching?
items.explanation: Magnetic force can act at a distance and through some materials, like paper. That is why the paperclip moves.

items.prompt: At a recycling centre, a big magnet lifts some cans out of a pile. Which cans does it lift?

options.why: Aluminium is a metal, but it is not magnetic.
Plastic is not magnetic.
Glass is not magnetic.

hints: The magnet only lifts magnetic materials.
Some metals are magnetic and some are not.
Which metal contains iron?
items.explanation: Steel contains iron, so steel cans are magnetic. Aluminium cans are not, so a magnet helps sort them.

items.prompt: Kevin counts how many paperclips each magnet can hold in a chain. What can he conclude?

head: Magnet
Size
Paperclips held
figure.alt: Table: magnet A is big and holds 5 paperclips. B is small and holds 12. C is medium and holds 8. D is big and holds 3.

options.text: A bigger magnet is not always stronger.

options.why: Magnet B is small but holds the most paperclips.
The magnets held between 3 and 12 paperclips.
Magnet D held only 3 paperclips, the fewest.

hints: The number of paperclips shows how strong each magnet is.
Find the strongest magnet. How big is it?
Compare the sizes with the numbers.
items.explanation: Magnet B is small but held 12 paperclips, the most. So the size of a magnet does not tell you how strong it is.

items.prompt: A compass needle is a tiny magnet. Why does it point north?

options.text: It is pulled towards the Sun.
options.why: The Sun does not pull the compass needle.

options.text: The Earth acts like a giant magnet.

options.why: A compass works indoors, with no wind.

options.text: It points to the nearest metal.
options.why: Nearby iron can pull a needle off course, but that is not why it points north.

hints: A magnet lines up with other magnets nearby.
Think about the biggest magnet you live on.
What could be magnetic all around the world?
items.explanation: The Earth behaves like a giant magnet. A compass needle lines up with the Earth's magnetism, so one end points north.

items.prompt: Choose 2 metals that a magnet will attract.

options.why: Aluminium is a metal, but it is not magnetic.
Copper is a metal, but it is not magnetic.
Gold is a metal, but it is not magnetic.

hints: Not every metal is magnetic.
Think about what nails and paperclips are made of.
One answer is mostly made from the other.
items.explanation: Iron and steel are magnetic, and steel is made mostly from iron. Aluminium, copper and gold are not magnetic.

items.prompt: End A of a magnet is a north pole. End A attracts end B of another magnet. End A repels end C of a third magnet. What are B and C?

options.text: B is south and C is north.
B is north and C is south.
options.why: End A is north. Opposite poles attract, so B must be south.

options.text: B and C are both north.
options.why: B attracts A, so B must be the opposite pole: south.

options.text: B and C are both south.
options.why: C repels A, so C must be the same pole as A: north.

hints: Attract means the poles are different.
Repel means the poles are the same.
Start with B. What is the opposite of north?
items.explanation: End A is north. B attracts A, so B is the opposite pole, south. C repels A, so C is the same pole, north.

items.prompt: Draw two bar magnets that will attract each other. Label the N and S poles.

criteria.label: Labels N and S on both magnets
The facing ends are opposite poles

hints: Each magnet has an N end and an S end.
Opposite poles attract.
items.explanation: The magnets attract when a north pole faces a south pole.

items.prompt: Which things are magnetic? Write Yes or No.
hints: A magnet pulls on some metals.
A plastic spoon is not a metal.
An iron nail is a magnetic metal.
items.explanation: An iron nail is magnetic. A plastic spoon and a wooden block are not.
